documents.title: Synthetic FCG: Buffer Boundaries
documents.content:
# Synthetic FCG: Buffer Boundaries

Dataset version 2.0.0. Illustrative research rules only; not official WD requirements.

In this section a capacity is the number of writable elements, not the last valid
index. [SFCG-019] A loop writing an array must keep each index strictly below
capacity. [SFCG-020] When reserving a header and payload, check for arithmetic
overflow before adding their lengths and compare the total with capacity.

For text output, [SFCG-021] reserve room for a terminating zero byte before
writing it, including the empty-text path. A ring queue follows a different rule:
[SFCG-022] compute the next head and reject insertion when it would equal the tail.

The DMA contract adds two constraints. [SFCG-023] Before scheduling DMA, require
four-byte alignment of both address and byte count. [SFCG-024] A byte count returned
by an external read must be capped at destination capacity before copying.

The empty-text exception does not permit writing a terminator into a zero-capacity
buffer. Consult `pointers.md` for null pointers with zero length.

documents.title: Synthetic FCG: Pointer Contracts
documents.content:
# Synthetic FCG: Pointer Contracts

Dataset version 2.0.0. Illustrative research rules only; not official WD requirements.
The following table applies to C firmware entry points receiving caller-owned memory.

| Rule | Requirement | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [SFCG-013] | Validate a required caller pointer before its first dereference. | Any entry point |
| [SFCG-014] | Reject a null output pointer before writing through it. | Output parameters |
| [SFCG-015] | Validate an externally supplied peripheral address against the allowed mapped range before MMIO access. | External addresses |
| [SFCG-016] | A null buffer is permitted when its length is zero; for a positive length the buffer must be non-null. | Length-bearing buffers |
| [SFCG-017] | Validate callback context before dereferencing it inside the callback. | Indirect callbacks |
| [SFCG-018] | Reject overlapping source and destination ranges when the operation contract forbids aliasing. | Copy without overlap support |

The zero-length exception in [SFCG-016] is intentional. It does not relax
[SFCG-013] for a separately required configuration pointer.

documents.title: Synthetic FCG: API Results and Calls
documents.content:
# Synthetic FCG: API Results and Calls

Dataset version 2.0.0. Illustrative research rules only; these are not official WD requirements.
Scope: C firmware in the synthetic benchmark. "Status" means the integer outcome returned
by a fallible operation; zero means success unless a local API declaration says otherwise.

1. [SFCG-001] After `sensor_open` succeeds, the returned handle may be used; a failed
   open must be handled before any handle access.
2. [SFCG-002] Firmware must inspect the result of `flash_write`, including a short
   write, before treating the bytes as stored.
3. [SFCG-003] A negative result from `adc_read` is an error and must not be cast into
   a sample value.
4. [SFCG-004] When a callback is invoked through a function pointer and its contract
   returns status, the caller must inspect that status before continuing.
5. [SFCG-005] A call declared infallible in the local interface has no status to test;
   do not invent a failure path solely for that call.
6. [SFCG-006] Failure of a best-effort diagnostic log operation may be ignored only
   when the caller does not depend on the log being persisted.

The exceptions in items 5 and 6 do not exempt `sensor_open`, `flash_write`, or
`adc_read` from their stated result-handling obligations. See `error_flow.md` for
propagation after a failed call.

#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdint.h>
size_t external_read_count(void);
void copy_samples(uint8_t *dst, const uint8_t *src, size_t capacity) {
    if (dst == NULL || src == NULL) return;
    size_t count = external_read_count();
    if (count > capacity) count = capacity;
    for (size_t i = 0; i < count; ++i) dst[i] = src[i];
}
